anomalies.title: A per-token-only prefill model fails on cache hits
anomalies.evidence: 8 cache-hit calls evaluated 1 token(s) yet prefill took 34.7 ms on average; 7.23 ms/token predicts 7.2 ms (5× too low).
anomalies.consequence: Model prefill as fixed + per-token: 30.7 ms + 6.15 ms/token. The fixed part bounds what caching can save per call.

anomalies.title: Decode has a negative fixed cost
anomalies.evidence: decode_ms ≈ -32.1 ms + 36.14 ms × output tokens; the intercept is about 0.9 tokens' worth below zero.
anomalies.consequence: Physically a call can't save time, so the server's decode timer likely excludes some generated tokens (e.g. the first one, sampled at the end of prefill). Untested hypothesis; it doesn't affect the per-token slope, but don't read decode_ms/completion_tokens as exact for short outputs.

anomalies.title: Some runs stopped at end-of-sequence before max_tokens
anomalies.evidence: 1 run(s) generated fewer tokens than max_tokens without --ignore-eos.
anomalies.consequence: Their wall_ms measures answer length, not speed. The decode line uses actual completion_tokens, so it is unaffected; per-run tok/s comparisons are not.

anomalies.title: The model critic approves wrong answers
anomalies.evidence: 3 false accept(s) over 10 episodes (critic=model window=all cache=false temp=0); success 50% vs baseline 50%.
anomalies.consequence: A same-model critic is not an independent check here; its calls are pure cost unless success rises.

anomalies.title: Agent wall time did not reproduce across runs of critic=none window=all cache=true temp=0
anomalies.evidence: 2 runs: 2468 ms/task at 37 prompt tokens/call vs 4894 ms/task at 31 prompt tokens/call.
anomalies.consequence: Something outside the recorded settings changed between runs (server state, background load, thermals). Pooled effects for this config carry that variance; replicate before trusting them.

failure_modes.rule: failed with no format or tool errors — the plan (expression) was wrong
failed, ≥1 format error, hit the 6-step limit
failed and the calculator rejected ≥1 expression

systematic_failures: task0 solved 0/8 episodes across all 6 configs: “A crate holds 12 boxes and each box holds 24 bolts. How many bolts are in 7 crates?”
task1 solved 0/8 episodes across all 6 configs: “A server handles 340 requests per minute. How many requests does it handle in 3 hours?”
task3 solved 0/8 episodes across all 6 configs: “A model generates 45 tokens per second. How many tokens does it generate in 8 minutes?”
task8 solved 0/8 episodes across all 6 configs: “A batch job processes 125 files per run and runs 6 times a day. How many files in 2 weeks?”
task9 solved 0/8 episodes across all 6 configs: “A 4096-token context is split into chunks of 256 tokens. How many chunks, minus the 3 reserved ones?”
methods: Lines (prefill vs evaluated prompt tokens, decode vs output tokens): Theil–Sen — median of pairwise slopes, intercept = median residual. Robust to warm-up outliers; no tuning constant.
Intervals: 95% percentile bootstrap, 200 resamples, fixed seed 7. Same notebook ⇒ same beliefs.
Success rates: Wilson score interval. Agent effects: difference of per-episode means vs the baseline config, two-sample bootstrap (unpaired; tasks are the same, so this is conservative).
Agent configs use only runs over the full 10-task set; subset runs are excluded so success rates are comparable.
Prefix-cache hit: cache_prompt=true and ≤4 evaluated prompt tokens. Modelled as paying only the fixed prefill cost.
Status: parameters are KNOWN when the 95% half-width ≤ 15% of the estimate; effects are KNOWN when the interval excludes zero.

Failure modes are rules over episode metrics, not clustering: solved; wrong answer (no format/tool errors: a planning error, since the calculator is exact); format loop (format errors until the step limit); format error then wrong answer; tool error.
40 agent episodes predate the tool_errors metric; their tool errors count as 0, so 'tool error' may be under-counted.
